targets.researchQuestion: Assemble current ATM/warrant/SBC dilution capacity and cash-burn runway from the Q2 2026 10-Q and quantify customer concentration.
targets.summary: RESOLVED for Chief review from the June 30, 2026 Form 10-Q. Liquidity, burn, ATM capacity, warrants, SBC and customer concentration are all explicitly quantified in the primary filing.

findings.fact: June 30 liquidity was $240.4M: $79.1M cash, $156.3M short-term marketable securities and $5.0M long-term marketable securities. Management states these resources are expected to fund working capital and capex for at least 12 months.
Six-month 2026 operating cash use was $84.738M versus $25.426M in the prior-year period; net loss was $113.131M.
The May 11, 2026 ATM authorized up to $150M. By June 30 SERV had sold 8,540,900 shares at a $9.08 weighted-average price for $77.6M gross/$75.2M net, leaving approximately $72.4M capacity.
Under the older 2025 ATM, SERV sold 1,217,000 shares in H1 2026 for $10.0M gross; inception-to-date through June 30 it had sold 7,716,935 shares for $91.2M gross.
5,079,294 warrants were outstanding and exercisable at June 30, 2026 at a weighted-average $10.18 exercise price; 4,000,000 of these are Vayu-related warrants at $10.36 expiring August 15, 2031.
H1 2026 stock-based compensation was $22.038M; unamortized compensation cost on unvested RSUs was $92.3M over an expected weighted-average 2.8 years.
Revenue concentration in Q2 2026 was Customer A 11% and Customer B 22%; for H1 2026 Customer A was 12% and Customer B 17%.
SERV has meaningful near-term liquidity but remains materially equity-financing dependent; the evidence supports explicit dilution/survival risk treatment rather than leaving the factor unknown.

contradictions: Management's at-least-12-month liquidity statement coexists with sharply higher operating cash burn and active ATM issuance; neither should erase the other.
unknowns: Customer A/B identities are not disclosed in the concentration table; exact identity is not required to quantify concentration.
falsifiers: A subsequent filing materially changing ATM capacity, warrant count, liquidity or customer concentration before Chief promotion.
